question: On 5 November 2025, the Expert Group on Climate Change Policy published the revised limits on free CO2 allowances for sectors deemed at risk of carbon leakage. The revised limits are particularly ambitious for sectors such as the ceramic industry and thermal-intensive sectors, with reductions of 50 % or very nearly 50 %.

Free allocation protects local industries and prevents relocation through the concept of ‘risk of carbon leakage’. However, it is proposed that this system be abolished, despite the continued risk of carbon leakage.

Sectors such as the ceramic tile industry do not have any real technological alternatives, nor do the regions in which they are concentrated (EmiliaRomagna in Italy and Castellón in Spain) have the electricity infrastructure and networks that would enable their electrification. Abolishing free allocation spells doom for those sectors’ competitiveness and removes all incentive for them to remain in Europe. 1.
What does the Commission intend to do to safeguard the interests of those sectors and protect the jobs of over 200 000 families?

Does the Commission plan to introduce any real, short-term mechanisms to ensure the competitiveness of the sector under the EU ETS, for which conditions that are in line with the sector’s technological advancement are essential?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.7.2026) The Emission Trading System (ETS) legislation provides for transitional free allocation to evolve and decline in time. The reduction rates are in line with the objective of economy-wide climate neutrality by 2050 and the interim reduction targets. The benchmark update exercise, including the applied methodology, is a legal obligation enshrined in the ETS Directive.

All flexibilities available have been taken on board and the Commission had no discretion to deviate from the existing legal framework without creating uncertainty and imposing a significant delay to the process of determining and transferring the 2026 free allocation to industry1.

Against this background, the Climate Change Committee gave a favourable opinion on the Benchmark Regulation2, including a commitment where the Commission will propose a separate amendment targeting the 2026-2030 allocation period and aiming at increasing the free allocation determined on the basis of the fall-back benchmarks, largely relevant for the ceramics sector, while at the same time avoiding the application of the cross-sectionalcorrection factor.
1 Article 10a(2) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a system

for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Union and amending Council Directive 96/61/EC, OJ L 275, 25.10.2003, p. 32, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2003/87/oj. 2 Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1412 of 26 June 2026 determining revised benchmark values for free allocation of emission allowances for the period from 2026 to 2030 pursuant to Article 10a(2) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council. ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/1412/oj.
